chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) it is narrated that Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to them from Muhammad ibn Humran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The free person and the slave do not inherit from each other."

The meaning in these narrations is that the free person and the slave do not inherit from each other, meaning that each one inherits the other, because the slave owns nothing, so the free person inherits him, and he (the slave) does not inherit the free person unless there is no one else (among the free). As for when there is someone else among the free people, then there is no mutual inheritance between them in any case.
ai.seo_question: How does inheritance work between a free person and a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the asymmetrical inheritance dynamics between a free person (*al-hurr*) and a slave (*al-mamluk*), rooted in the slave's lack of independent property ownership. The juristic resolution explains that while the free person inherits the slave's estate, the slave only inherits the free person in the absence of other free heirs, otherwise precluding mutual inheritance. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential understanding of *'asl al-mirath* (root of inheritance) and the legal status of slaves in early Islamic society.
